existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-b-convention
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: The system \(KTB\), the schema B, and the alias \(B\)
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Chellas writes \(KTB\) for the reflexive symmetric modal-cube system: it
contains both the T schema and the B schema.  The B schema alone corresponds
to symmetry, and Chellas writes \(KB\) for the strictly weaker system obtained
by adding only that schema to \(K\) \cite{Chellas1980}.  Hughes and Cresswell
use \(B\) as a name for the reflexive symmetric system
\cite{HughesCresswell1996}; here \(B\) is therefore recorded only as their
source-bound alias for the card whose Chellas name is \(KTB\).

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-canonical-model
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Canonical-model method
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
\index{canonical-model method!modal logic}
For a fixed normal modal logic \(\mathfrak L\), let the worlds be the maximal
\(\mathfrak L\)-consistent sets.  Define the metalinguistic proof relation
\(R_{\mathfrak L}\) by
\[
 \Gamma R_{\mathfrak L}\Delta
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \forall A\,(\Box A\in\Gamma\to A\in\Delta),
\]
and make an atom true at \(\Gamma\) exactly when it belongs to \(\Gamma\).
This construction is needed to distinguish the proof model from an arbitrary
semantic structure.  Its worlds are theories, unlike filtration worlds, which
are equivalence classes of worlds from a given model.  The relation is used by
the modal existence lemma, truth lemma, and the frame-property checks in the
following adequacy sketch.  The ordinary construction applies to the canonical
systems \(K\), \(KD\), \(KT\), \(KTB\), \(K4\), \(S4\) (\(KT4\)),
\(KD45\), \(S4.2\), \(S4.3\), and \(S5\) with their source-defined
schemas; it is not the completeness route asserted for GL or Grz.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-modal-canonical-completeness
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Canonical strong completeness for \(K\), \(KT\), \(S4\), and \(S5\)
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For each of the four exact Hilbert sheets
\texttt{sheet:hilbert-k}, \texttt{sheet:hilbert-t},
\texttt{sheet:hilbert-s4}, and \texttt{sheet:hilbert-s5}, derivability from an
arbitrary premise set is equivalent to local consequence over, respectively,
all frames, reflexive frames, reflexive transitive frames, and equivalence
frames.  Necessitation remains theorem-only in premise derivations.

current_declaration_bindings.title: The system \(KTB\), the schema B, and the alias \(B\)
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Chellas writes \(KTB\) for the reflexive symmetric modal-cube system: it
contains both the T schema and the B schema.  The B schema alone corresponds
to symmetry, and Chellas writes \(KB\) for the strictly weaker system obtained
by adding only that schema to \(K\) \cite{Chellas1980}.  Hughes and Cresswell
use \(B\) as a name for the reflexive symmetric system
\cite{HughesCresswell1996}; here \(B\) is therefore recorded only as their
source-bound alias for the card whose Chellas name is \(KTB\).

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-modal-canonical-model
current_declaration_bindings.title: Canonical-model method
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
\index{canonical-model method!modal logic}
For a fixed normal modal logic \(\mathfrak L\), let the worlds be the maximal
\(\mathfrak L\)-consistent sets.  Define the metalinguistic proof relation
\(R_{\mathfrak L}\) by
\[
 \Gamma R_{\mathfrak L}\Delta
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \forall A\,(\Box A\in\Gamma\to A\in\Delta),
\]
and make an atom true at \(\Gamma\) exactly when it belongs to \(\Gamma\).
This construction is needed to distinguish the proof model from an arbitrary
semantic structure.  Its worlds are theories, unlike filtration worlds, which
are equivalence classes of worlds from a given model.  The relation is used by
the modal existence lemma, truth lemma, and the frame-property checks in the
following adequacy sketch.  The ordinary construction applies to the canonical
systems \(K\), \(KD\), \(KT\), \(KTB\), \(K4\), \(S4\) (\(KT4\)),
\(KD45\), \(S4.2\), \(S4.3\), and \(S5\) with their source-defined
schemas; it is not the completeness route asserted for GL or Grz.

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-modal-canonical-completeness
current_declaration_bindings.title: Canonical strong completeness for \(K\), \(KT\), \(S4\), and \(S5\)
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
For each of the four exact Hilbert sheets
\texttt{sheet:hilbert-k}, \texttt{sheet:hilbert-t},
\texttt{sheet:hilbert-s4}, and \texttt{sheet:hilbert-s5}, derivability from an
arbitrary premise set is equivalent to local consequence over, respectively,
all frames, reflexive frames, reflexive transitive frames, and equivalence
frames.  Necessitation remains theorem-only in premise derivations.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-standard-translation
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: First-order standard translation
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For each propositional variable \(p\), choose a unary predicate symbol
\(P_p\).  The standard translation at the displayed free world variable
\(x\), written \(\operatorname{ST}_x\), is the metalinguistic recursion
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{ST}_x(p)&=P_p(x),
 &\operatorname{ST}_x(\bottom)&=\bottom,\\
 \operatorname{ST}_x(\neg A)&=\neg\operatorname{ST}_x(A),
 &\operatorname{ST}_x(A\circ B)&=
   \operatorname{ST}_x(A)\circ\operatorname{ST}_x(B),\\
 \operatorname{ST}_x(\Box A)&=
   \forall y\,(Rxy\to\operatorname{ST}_y(A)),
 &\operatorname{ST}_x(\Diamond A)&=
   \exists y\,(Rxy\land\operatorname{ST}_y(A)),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(\circ\in\{\land,\lor,\to\}\) and \(y\) is fresh.  This is a
translation into first-order formulas over the frame relation and valuation
predicates, not a new modal connective.  It is needed to state the exact frame
conditions below and later to formulate the bisimulation characterization.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-modal-correspondence
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Elementary modal frame correspondences
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For every Kripke frame, validity of each named schema in the first column of
Table~\ref{tab:p08-modal-correspondence} is equivalent to the displayed
first-order condition on its accessibility relation.  The row named B concerns
the B schema alone; the displayed system \(KTB\) additionally contains T and
hence uses reflexive symmetric frames.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-sahlqvist-class
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: The Sahlqvist class used here
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Rewrite modal formulas using \(\bottom,\topv,\neg,\land,\lor,\Box,\Diamond\).
An occurrence of a variable is positive when it lies under an even number of
negations and negative when it lies under an odd number.  A \emph{boxed atom}
is \(\Box^n p\) for \(n\geq0\).  A \emph{Sahlqvist antecedent} is generated
from boxed atoms, formulas all of whose variable occurrences are negative,
and \(\bottom,\topv\) by \(\land,\lor,\Diamond\).  A \emph{Sahlqvist
implication} has such an antecedent and a consequent all of whose variable
occurrences are positive; finite conjunctions of these implications form the
Sahlqvist class fixed here.  This exact syntactic class is narrower than the
class of all modal formulas and is introduced because the following theorem
does not hold for arbitrary schemas.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-sahlqvist
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Sahlqvist theorem
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Every formula in the class fixed by
Definition~\ref{def:p08-sahlqvist-class} has an effectively computable
first-order frame correspondent, is canonical, and axiomatizes a normal modal
logic complete for the corresponding elementary frame class.  No claim is
made here that an arbitrary modal axiom is a Sahlqvist formula.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-standard-translation
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: First-order standard translation
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For each propositional variable \(p\), choose a unary predicate symbol
\(P_p\).  The standard translation at the displayed free world variable
\(x\), written \(\operatorname{ST}_x\), is the metalinguistic recursion
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{ST}_x(p)&=P_p(x),
 &\operatorname{ST}_x(\bottom)&=\bottom,\\
 \operatorname{ST}_x(\neg A)&=\neg\operatorname{ST}_x(A),
 &\operatorname{ST}_x(A\circ B)&=
   \operatorname{ST}_x(A)\circ\operatorname{ST}_x(B),\\
 \operatorname{ST}_x(\Box A)&=
   \forall y\,(Rxy\to\operatorname{ST}_y(A)),
 &\operatorname{ST}_x(\Diamond A)&=
   \exists y\,(Rxy\land\operatorname{ST}_y(A)),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(\circ\in\{\land,\lor,\to\}\) and \(y\) is fresh.  This is a
translation into first-order formulas over the frame relation and valuation
predicates, not a new modal connective.  It is needed to state the exact frame
conditions below and later to formulate the bisimulation characterization.

existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Elementary modal frame correspondences
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For every Kripke frame, validity of each named schema in the first column of
Table~\ref{tab:p08-modal-correspondence} is equivalent to the displayed
first-order condition on its accessibility relation.  The row named B concerns
the B schema alone; the displayed system \(KTB\) additionally contains T and
hence uses reflexive symmetric frames.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-sahlqvist-class
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: The Sahlqvist class used here
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Rewrite modal formulas using \(\bottom,\topv,\neg,\land,\lor,\Box,\Diamond\).
An occurrence of a variable is positive when it lies under an even number of
negations and negative when it lies under an odd number.  A \emph{boxed atom}
is \(\Box^n p\) for \(n\geq0\).  A \emph{Sahlqvist antecedent} is generated
from boxed atoms, formulas all of whose variable occurrences are negative,
and \(\bottom,\topv\) by \(\land,\lor,\Diamond\).  A \emph{Sahlqvist
implication} has such an antecedent and a consequent all of whose variable
occurrences are positive; finite conjunctions of these implications form the
Sahlqvist class fixed here.  This exact syntactic class is narrower than the
class of all modal formulas and is introduced because the following theorem
does not hold for arbitrary schemas.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-modal-bisimulation-invariance
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Bisimulation invariance
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
If \(wZw'\) for a bisimulation between \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal N\),
then for every basic modal formula \(A\),
\[
 \mathcal M,w\entails A
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \mathcal N,w'\entails A.
\]

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-van-benthem
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Van Benthem characterization theorem
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Over all Kripke structures, a first-order formula with one free world variable
is equivalent to \(\operatorname{ST}_x(A)\) for some basic modal formula
\(A\) exactly when it is invariant under bisimulations.  This statement is not
restricted to finite structures; the finite-model version is a different
theorem.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-filtration
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Filtration through a finite formula set
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
\index{filtration!modal logic}
Fix a finite subformula-closed set \(\Phi\) and a Kripke structure
\(\mathcal M=(W,R,V)\).  Put
\[
 w\sim_{\Phi}u
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \forall A\in\Phi\,
   (\mathcal M,w\entails A\text{ iff }\mathcal M,u\entails A).
\]
The quotient has worlds \([w]_{\Phi}\), at most \(2^{\lvert\Phi\rvert}\)
of them, and the induced atomic valuation.  The minimal quotient relation
relates \([w]_{\Phi}\) to \([u]_{\Phi}\) when some representatives are
\(R\)-related.  The maximal quotient relation relates them when, for every
\(\Box A\in\Phi\), truth of \(\Box A\) at \(w\) implies truth of \(A\) at
\(u\).  A \emph{filtration relation} is a quotient relation between those two
bounds.  This construction is an image of a given semantic model, unlike the
maximal-consistent-theory construction in
Method~\ref{def:p08-modal-canonical-model}; it is used to preserve truth on
\(\Phi\) while making the model finite.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-modal-filtration
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Filtration and decidability
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Every filtration as in Method~\ref{def:p08-modal-filtration} preserves the
truth of each formula in \(\Phi\).  For \(K\) use an ordinary filtration
relation; for \(KT\) use its reflexive closure; for \(S4\) use the standard
reflexive-transitive filtration construction; and for \(S5\) use the
equivalence-class construction.
In each case the declared filtration relation remains between the minimal and maximal
bounds and preserves the target frame class.  Hence \(K\), \(KT\), \(S4\),
and \(S5\) have the
finite-model property and are decidable
\cite{BlackburnDeRijkeVenema2001,ChagrovZakharyaschev1997}.  This is cited new
content: no local proof or inherited compression denominator is claimed.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-kripke-incomplete-logics
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Existence of Kripke-incomplete normal modal logics
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Thomason exhibited a normal modal logic that is not complete with respect to
any class of ordinary Kripke frames \cite{Thomason1974}.  Fine exhibited such
an incomplete normal extension containing S4 \cite{Fine1974}.  These two
existence results do not imply that every noncanonical logic is Kripke
incomplete; the broader boundary is surveyed in
\cite{ChagrovZakharyaschev1997}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-general-frame
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: General frame boundary
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
A \emph{general frame} is a triple \((W,R,\mathcal A)\), where
\((W,R)\) is a Kripke frame and \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P(W)\) is a
specified family of admissible proposition sets closed under the Boolean and
modal operations used by the language.  Validity restricts valuations to
members of \(\mathcal A\).  This extra admissible-set component distinguishes a
general frame from the ordinary frame of
Section~\ref{sec:modal-temporal-epistemic-01}; it is used to explain how
relational methods can represent logics missed by unrestricted Kripke
valuations.  No blanket claim that every noncanonical logic is repaired by one
fixed general-frame class is made.
The admissible-set semantics is historically connected with Scott's framework
\cite{Scott1970}; this definition does not identify general frames with the
neighborhood models below.

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-kripke-incomplete-logics
current_declaration_bindings.title: Existence of Kripke-incomplete normal modal logics
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Thomason exhibited a normal modal logic that is not complete with respect to
any class of ordinary Kripke frames \cite{Thomason1974}.  Fine exhibited such
an incomplete normal extension containing S4 \cite{Fine1974}.  These two
existence results do not imply that every noncanonical logic is Kripke
incomplete; the broader boundary is surveyed in
\cite{ChagrovZakharyaschev1997}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-general-frame
current_declaration_bindings.title: General frame boundary
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
A \emph{general frame} is a triple \((W,R,\mathcal A)\), where
\((W,R)\) is a Kripke frame and \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P(W)\) is a
specified family of admissible proposition sets closed under the Boolean and
modal operations used by the language.  Validity restricts valuations to
members of \(\mathcal A\).  This extra admissible-set component distinguishes a
general frame from the ordinary frame of
Section~\ref{sec:modal-temporal-epistemic-01}; it is used to explain how
relational methods can represent logics missed by unrestricted Kripke
valuations.  No blanket claim that every noncanonical logic is repaired by one
fixed general-frame class is made.
The admissible-set semantics is historically connected with Scott's framework
\cite{Scott1970}; this definition does not identify general frames with the
neighborhood models below.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-neighborhood-model
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Neighborhood model
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
A \emph{neighborhood model} is
\(\mathcal M=(W,N,V)\), where \(W\ne\varnothing\),
\(V:\mathsf{Prop}\to\mathcal P(W)\), and
\(N:W\to\mathcal P(\mathcal P(W))\).  For a formula \(A\), define
its truth-set abbreviation by
\(\lbrack\!\lbrack A\rbrack\!\rbrack_{\mathcal M}
\defeq\{w\in W:\mathcal M,w\entails A\}\).  The modal clause is
\[
 \mathcal M,w\entails\Box A
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \lbrack\!\lbrack A\rbrack\!\rbrack_{\mathcal M}\in N(w).
\]
The function \(N\) is needed because a single accessibility relation
cannot represent every congruential non-normal logic.  Its standing is a
semantic assignment of proposition sets to each world; it is neither the
system \(EN\) nor the set of normal worlds used in the later
Routley--Meyer structure.  It differs from a Kripke
relation by taking subsets of \(W\), rather than worlds, as its local semantic
arguments, and is used in all five cards below
\cite{Scott1970,Montague1970,Chellas1980,Pacuit2017}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-neighborhood-conditions
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Neighborhood closure conditions
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For every world \(w\) and \(X,Y\subseteq W\), call \(N\)
\emph{upward closed} when
\(X\in N(w)\) and \(X\subseteq Y\) imply
\(Y\in N(w)\); \emph{binary-intersection closed} when
\(X,Y\in N(w)\) implies
\(X\cap Y\in N(w)\); and \emph{unit containing} when
\(W\in N(w)\).  These are semantic frame conditions, not additional
object-language rules.  They are introduced separately because Chellas's
schemas M, C, and N determine different combinations of them
\cite{Chellas1980,Pacuit2017}.

current_declaration_bindings.title: Neighborhood model
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
A \emph{neighborhood model} is
\(\mathcal M=(W,N,V)\), where \(W\ne\varnothing\),
\(V:\mathsf{Prop}\to\mathcal P(W)\), and
\(N:W\to\mathcal P(\mathcal P(W))\).  For a formula \(A\), define
its truth-set abbreviation by
\(\lbrack\!\lbrack A\rbrack\!\rbrack_{\mathcal M}
\defeq\{w\in W:\mathcal M,w\entails A\}\).  The modal clause is
\[
 \mathcal M,w\entails\Box A
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \lbrack\!\lbrack A\rbrack\!\rbrack_{\mathcal M}\in N(w).
\]
The function \(N\) is needed because a single accessibility relation
cannot represent every congruential non-normal logic.  Its standing is a
semantic assignment of proposition sets to each world; it is neither the
system \(EN\) nor the set of normal worlds used in the later
Routley--Meyer structure.  It differs from a Kripke
relation by taking subsets of \(W\), rather than worlds, as its local semantic
arguments, and is used in all five cards below
\cite{Scott1970,Montague1970,Chellas1980,Pacuit2017}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-neighborhood-conditions
current_declaration_bindings.title: Neighborhood closure conditions
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
For every world \(w\) and \(X,Y\subseteq W\), call \(N\)
\emph{upward closed} when
\(X\in N(w)\) and \(X\subseteq Y\) imply
\(Y\in N(w)\); \emph{binary-intersection closed} when
\(X,Y\in N(w)\) implies
\(X\cap Y\in N(w)\); and \emph{unit containing} when
\(W\in N(w)\).  These are semantic frame conditions, not additional
object-language rules.  They are introduced separately because Chellas's
schemas M, C, and N determine different combinations of them
\cite{Chellas1980,Pacuit2017}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-b-convention
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: The system \(KTB\), the schema B, and the alias \(B\)
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Chellas writes \(KTB\) for the reflexive symmetric modal-cube system: it
contains both the T schema and the B schema.  The B schema alone corresponds
to symmetry, and Chellas writes \(KB\) for the strictly weaker system obtained
by adding only that schema to \(K\) \cite{Chellas1980}.  Hughes and Cresswell
use \(B\) as a name for the reflexive symmetric system
\cite{HughesCresswell1996}; here \(B\) is therefore recorded only as their
source-bound alias for the card whose Chellas name is \(KTB\).

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-modal-frame-properties
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Frame properties used in the system catalog
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For a modal frame \((W,R)\), the relation \(R\) is \emph{serial} when
\(\forall x\,\exists y\,Rxy\), \emph{Euclidean} when
\(\forall x\forall y\forall z\,(Rxy\land Rxz\to Ryz)\),
\emph{directed} (or \emph{convergent}) when
\(\forall x\forall y\forall z\,
(Rxy\land Rxz\to\exists u\,(Ryu\land Rzu))\), and
\emph{weakly connected} when
\(\forall x\forall y\forall z\,
(Rxy\land Rxz\to(Ryz\lor Rzy))\).  These are exact first-order
properties of the accessibility relation, not names for proof rules.  They are
needed because the catalog distinguishes \(KD\), \(KD45\), \(S4.2\), and
\(S4.3\) from systems
characterized only by reflexivity, symmetry, or transitivity; the same clauses
reappear in the correspondence table below.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-gl-arithmetical-completeness
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Arithmetical completeness of GL
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
An arithmetical realization maps propositional variables to closed
arithmetical sentences, commutes with the Boolean connectives, and interprets
\(\Box B\) by the standard provability predicate
\(\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathsf{PA}}\) applied to the G\"odel number of the realized
sentence \(B\).  A modal formula is derivable in GL exactly when its image
under every such arithmetical realization is derivable in \(\mathsf{PA}\).  This is an
arithmetical-interpretation theorem, not the finite-frame completeness claim on
the GL card \cite{Boolos1993}.

Chellas writes \(KTB\) for the reflexive symmetric modal-cube system: it
contains both the T schema and the B schema.  The B schema alone corresponds
to symmetry, and Chellas writes \(KB\) for the strictly weaker system obtained
by adding only that schema to \(K\) \cite{Chellas1980}.  Hughes and Cresswell

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-modal-frame-properties
current_declaration_bindings.title: Frame properties used in the system catalog
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
For a modal frame \((W,R)\), the relation \(R\) is \emph{serial} when
\(\forall x\,\exists y\,Rxy\), \emph{Euclidean} when
\(\forall x\forall y\forall z\,(Rxy\land Rxz\to Ryz)\),
\emph{directed} (or \emph{convergent}) when
\(\forall x\forall y\forall z\,
(Rxy\land Rxz\to\exists u\,(Ryu\land Rzu))\), and
\emph{weakly connected} when
\(\forall x\forall y\forall z\,
(Rxy\land Rxz\to(Ryz\lor Rzy))\).  These are exact first-order
properties of the accessibility relation, not names for proof rules.  They are
needed because the catalog distinguishes \(KD\), \(KD45\), \(S4.2\), and
\(S4.3\) from systems
characterized only by reflexivity, symmetry, or transitivity; the same clauses
reappear in the correspondence table below.

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-gl-arithmetical-completeness
current_declaration_bindings.title: Arithmetical completeness of GL
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
An arithmetical realization maps propositional variables to closed
arithmetical sentences, commutes with the Boolean connectives, and interprets
\(\Box B\) by the standard provability predicate
\(\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathsf{PA}}\) applied to the G\"odel number of the realized
sentence \(B\).  A modal formula is derivable in GL exactly when its image
under every such arithmetical realization is derivable in \(\mathsf{PA}\).  This is an
arithmetical-interpretation theorem, not the finite-frame completeness claim on
the GL card \cite{Boolos1993}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-two-index-actuality
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Davies--Humberstone's source operators \(A\) and \(\mathcal F\)
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Davies and Humberstone's two-index presentation of \(S5\) uses a
model \(\langle W,V\rangle\) and writes truth as
\(\langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\alpha\).  The lower index \(x\) is the
world of evaluation and the upper index \(y\) is the actual-world
perspective.  For atoms and the three modal operators used here, their clauses
are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y p
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad V(p,x)=1,\\
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\Box\alpha
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad
   \forall z\in W\;\langle W,V\rangle\models_z^y\alpha,\\
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y A\alpha
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad
   \langle W,V\rangle\models_y^y\alpha,\\
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\mathcal F\alpha
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad
   \forall z\in W\;\langle W,V\rangle\models_x^z\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
Boolean clauses are evaluated at the displayed indices.  Here \(A\) is the
source actuality operator and \(\mathcal F\) is the source fixedly operator;

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-two-index-actuality
current_declaration_bindings.title: Davies--Humberstone's source operators \(A\) and \(\mathcal F\)
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Davies and Humberstone's two-index presentation of \(S5\) uses a
model \(\langle W,V\rangle\) and writes truth as
\(\langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\alpha\).  The lower index \(x\) is the
world of evaluation and the upper index \(y\) is the actual-world
perspective.  For atoms and the three modal operators used here, their clauses
are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y p
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad V(p,x)=1,\\
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\Box\alpha
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad
   \forall z\in W\;\langle W,V\rangle\models_z^y\alpha,\\
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y A\alpha
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad
   \langle W,V\rangle\models_y^y\alpha,\\
 \langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\mathcal F\alpha
 &\quad\text{ iff }\quad
   \forall z\in W\;\langle W,V\rangle\models_x^z\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
Boolean clauses are evaluated at the displayed indices.  Here \(A\) is the
source actuality operator and \(\mathcal F\) is the source fixedly operator;
within this definition they are unary object-language operators, while
\(\alpha\) is the source formula metavariable.  The extra index is necessary
because one index cannot record both the evaluation world and the actual-world
perspective.  The operators are nonredundant with \(\Box\): the S5 box varies
the lower evaluation index, \(A\) resets it to the upper actual-world index,
and \(\mathcal F\) instead varies the upper index while holding the lower one
fixed.  These distinctions separate actuality from the two notions of
necessity studied in the cited systems
\cite{CrossleyHumberstone1977,DaviesHumberstone1980}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-character-content
current_declaration_bindings.title: Context, character, and content
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
In Kaplan's terminology, a sentence occurrence's \emph{character} is its rule
from contexts to contents, while a \emph{content} is what that rule supplies at
one context and is evaluated at a circumstance.  A context may contain an
agent, time, place, and world; only its world component is used in the present
comparison.  Thus, if context \(c\) designates \(y\), the content expressed by
formula \(\alpha\) at \(c\) is true at circumstance \(x\) exactly when
\(\langle W,V\rangle\models_x^y\alpha\).  Diagonal evaluation uses \(x=y\),
so it is true exactly when
\(\langle W,V\rangle\models_y^y\alpha\).  These are metalinguistic semantic
levels, not additional operators or newly named maps.  Character cannot replace
content because it still awaits a context, and content cannot replace character
because it no longer varies with context.  The distinction is used immediately
to state the two-dimensional payoff \cite{Kaplan1989}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-family
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Quantified modal logic is a parameterized family
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
There is no single calculus or semantics determined by the phrase
``quantified modal logic.''  A source presentation must specify its
propositional modal base, quantifier rules, domain variation, designation
policy, and local or global consequence.  The clauses below reproduce
Fitting's model and quantifier notation for the limited purpose of comparing
the actualist Barcan schemas; Garson is used only for the surrounding
comparison with other quantified-modal presentations.  No hybrid calculus or
system card is inferred from that semantic example
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998,Garson2001}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-model
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Fitting's varying-domain modal model
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
In Fitting's notation a model is
\[
 \mathcal M=\langle\mathcal G,\mathcal R,\mathcal D,\mathcal I\rangle,
\]
where \(\mathcal G\) is a nonempty set of worlds,
\(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal G^2\), and
\(\mathcal D\) maps each \(\Gamma\in\mathcal G\) to a nonempty world-domain
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The domain of the model is
\(\bigcup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal G}\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The interpretation
\(\mathcal I\) maps each predicate symbol \(P\) to its world-relative
extension \(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)\) over that model domain and each individual
constant \(c\) to a world-indexed denotation
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)\) in the model domain.  A constant is a
\emph{rigid designator} exactly when some \(d\) satisfies
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)=d\) at every world \(\Gamma\).  Rigidity concerns
cross-world identity of denotation; whether \(d\in\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) is the
separate actual-existence question expressed by \(E(c)\).  The Barcan formulas
below contain variables rather than constants, so their proof uses the fixed
valuation convention and does not assume that every name is rigid.
The term is necessary because a world-independent variable assignment does not
fix the denotation policy for names.  Its standing is a property of a constant's
interpretation, and its nonredundancy from existence is used when rigid names
denote objects outside a current world-domain.  For Fitting's special
existence predicate \(E\),
\[
 \mathcal I(E)(\Gamma)=\mathcal D(\Gamma).
\]
Valuations \(v\) take variables into the model domain and do not vary with the
world.  For a formula \(\Phi\), truth is written
\(\mathcal M,\Gamma\forces_v\Phi\).  Ordinary
\((\forall x)\) and \((\exists x)\) are possibilist and range over the whole
model domain.  Fitting's actualist quantifiers are the exact abbreviations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (\forall^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\forall x)[E(x)\supset\Phi],\\
 (\exists^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\exists x)[E(x)\land\Phi].
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the relativized quantifiers range over \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) at world
\(\Gamma\), while modal satisfaction keeps \(v\) fixed when it moves along
\(\mathcal R\).  The model-domain convention is necessary to state
decreasing-domain failures with one world-independent valuation
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-domain-regimes
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Domain regimes and philosophical readings
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
The domains are \emph{constant} when \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) has the same
value at every world; \emph{increasing} when
\(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Delta)\);
\emph{decreasing} when \(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Gamma)\); and
\emph{arbitrarily varying} when no inclusion condition is imposed.  In this
section, \emph{actualist quantification} means Fitting's relativized
\(\forall^E,\exists^E\), while the primitive unrelativized quantifiers are
\emph{possibilist}; and the domain assignment is \emph{necessitist} exactly
when every world-domain is the whole model domain.  These are explicitly defined
interpretations of the semantic parameters, not consequences of the validity
table below.  The displayed BF/CBF table uses the actualist clauses.  Under
possibilist quantification over the model domain, varying the world-domains does not
generate that table; under necessitism, actualist and possibilist
quantification coincide with the constant-domain case.  This is the later use
that requires the three readings to remain distinct \cite{Williamson2013}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-barcan-schemas
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Barcan and converse Barcan schemas
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For a formula \(\Phi(x)\), the actualist \emph{Barcan formula}
\((\mathrm{BF}^{E})\) and actualist \emph{converse Barcan formula}
\((\mathrm{CBF}^{E})\) in Fitting's notation are respectively
\[
 (\forall^{E}x)\Box\Phi(x)\to\Box(\forall^{E}x)\Phi(x),
 \qquad
 \Box(\forall^{E}x)\Phi(x)\to(\forall^{E}x)\Box\Phi(x).
\]
The superscript records that this table uses the source's actualist
relativization.  With the primitive possibilist quantifier, local-domain
variation does not yield the table below.  The two names remain in this order;
their difference
is used in Table~\ref{tab:p08-barcan-domains} and
Figure~\ref{fig:p08-barcan-countermodel}; they are not interchanged when the
domain convention changes \cite{Barcan1946}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-barcan-domain-validities
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Actualist Barcan validity in Fitting's model
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Under Definitions~\ref{def:p08-qml-model}--\ref{def:p08-barcan-schemas}, the
validity pattern is exactly that displayed in
Table~\ref{tab:p08-barcan-domains}.  The decreasing-domain row uses the fixed
outer domain and fixed-variable-assignment convention; without such a convention the
reversal is not a well-formed comparison.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-barcan-countermodel
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Increasing-domain failure of BF
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Let \(\mathcal G=\{\Gamma,\Delta\}\) and
\(\mathcal R=\{(\Gamma,\Delta)\}\).  Take
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)=\{a\}\),
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)=\{a,b\}\),
\(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)=\varnothing\), and
\(\mathcal I(P)(\Delta)=\{a\}\).  Thus at \(\Delta\), \(P(a)\) is true and
\(P(b)\) is false.  At \(\Gamma\),
\((\forall^{E}x)\Box P(x)\) is true because the sole root-domain
object \(a\) satisfies \(P\) at the accessible world.  But
\(\Box(\forall^{E}x)P(x)\) is false because the new object
\(b\in\mathcal D(\Delta)\) fails \(P\) there.  Thus the model refutes
\(\mathrm{BF}^{E}\).  It does not refute \(\mathrm{CBF}^{E}\).

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-qml-model
current_declaration_bindings.title: Fitting's varying-domain modal model
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
In Fitting's notation a model is
\[
 \mathcal M=\langle\mathcal G,\mathcal R,\mathcal D,\mathcal I\rangle,
\]
where \(\mathcal G\) is a nonempty set of worlds,
\(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal G^2\), and
\(\mathcal D\) maps each \(\Gamma\in\mathcal G\) to a nonempty world-domain
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The domain of the model is
\(\bigcup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal G}\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The interpretation
\(\mathcal I\) maps each predicate symbol \(P\) to its world-relative
extension \(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)\) over that model domain and each individual
constant \(c\) to a world-indexed denotation
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)\) in the model domain.  A constant is a
\emph{rigid designator} exactly when some \(d\) satisfies
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)=d\) at every world \(\Gamma\).  Rigidity concerns
cross-world identity of denotation; whether \(d\in\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) is the
separate actual-existence question expressed by \(E(c)\).  The Barcan formulas
below contain variables rather than constants, so their proof uses the fixed
valuation convention and does not assume that every name is rigid.
The term is necessary because a world-independent variable assignment does not
fix the denotation policy for names.  Its standing is a property of a constant's
interpretation, and its nonredundancy from existence is used when rigid names
denote objects outside a current world-domain.  For Fitting's special
existence predicate \(E\),
\[
 \mathcal I(E)(\Gamma)=\mathcal D(\Gamma).
\]
Valuations \(v\) take variables into the model domain and do not vary with the
world.  For a formula \(\Phi\), truth is written
\(\mathcal M,\Gamma\forces_v\Phi\).  Ordinary
\((\forall x)\) and \((\exists x)\) are possibilist and range over the whole
model domain.  Fitting's actualist quantifiers are the exact abbreviations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (\forall^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\forall x)[E(x)\supset\Phi],\\
 (\exists^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\exists x)[E(x)\land\Phi].
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the relativized quantifiers range over \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) at world
\(\Gamma\), while modal satisfaction keeps \(v\) fixed when it moves along
\(\mathcal R\).  The model-domain convention is necessary to state
decreasing-domain failures with one world-independent valuation
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-qml-domain-regimes
current_declaration_bindings.title: Domain regimes and philosophical readings
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
The domains are \emph{constant} when \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) has the same
value at every world; \emph{increasing} when
\(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Delta)\);
\emph{decreasing} when \(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Gamma)\); and
\emph{arbitrarily varying} when no inclusion condition is imposed.  In this
section, \emph{actualist quantification} means Fitting's relativized
\(\forall^E,\exists^E\), while the primitive unrelativized quantifiers are
\emph{possibilist}; and the domain assignment is \emph{necessitist} exactly
when every world-domain is the whole model domain.  These are explicitly defined
interpretations of the semantic parameters, not consequences of the validity
table below.  The displayed BF/CBF table uses the actualist clauses.  Under
possibilist quantification over the model domain, varying the world-domains does not
generate that table; under necessitism, actualist and possibilist
quantification coincide with the constant-domain case.  This is the later use
that requires the three readings to remain distinct \cite{Williamson2013}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-barcan-schemas
current_declaration_bindings.title: Barcan and converse Barcan schemas
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
For a formula \(\Phi(x)\), the actualist \emph{Barcan formula}
\((\mathrm{BF}^{E})\) and actualist \emph{converse Barcan formula}
\((\mathrm{CBF}^{E})\) in Fitting's notation are respectively
\[
 (\forall^{E}x)\Box\Phi(x)\to\Box(\forall^{E}x)\Phi(x),
 \qquad
 \Box(\forall^{E}x)\Phi(x)\to(\forall^{E}x)\Box\Phi(x).
\]
The superscript records that this table uses the source's actualist
relativization.  With the primitive possibilist quantifier, local-domain
variation does not yield the table below.  The two names remain in this order;
their difference
is used in Table~\ref{tab:p08-barcan-domains} and
Figure~\ref{fig:p08-barcan-countermodel}; they are not interchanged when the
domain convention changes \cite{Barcan1946}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-barcan-domain-validities
current_declaration_bindings.title: Actualist Barcan validity in Fitting's model
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Under Definitions~\ref{def:p08-qml-model}--\ref{def:p08-barcan-schemas}, the
validity pattern is exactly that displayed in
Table~\ref{tab:p08-barcan-domains}.  The decreasing-domain row uses the fixed

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-barcan-countermodel
current_declaration_bindings.title: Increasing-domain failure of BF
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Let \(\mathcal G=\{\Gamma,\Delta\}\) and
\(\mathcal R=\{(\Gamma,\Delta)\}\).  Take
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)=\{a\}\),
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)=\{a,b\}\),
\(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)=\varnothing\), and
\(\mathcal I(P)(\Delta)=\{a\}\).  Thus at \(\Delta\), \(P(a)\) is true and
\(P(b)\) is false.  At \(\Gamma\),
\((\forall^{E}x)\Box P(x)\) is true because the sole root-domain
object \(a\) satisfies \(P\) at the accessible world.  But
\(\Box(\forall^{E}x)P(x)\) is false because the new object
\(b\in\mathcal D(\Delta)\) fails \(P\) there.  Thus the model refutes
\(\mathrm{BF}^{E}\).  It does not refute \(\mathrm{CBF}^{E}\).

existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Quantified modal logic is a parameterized family
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
There is no single calculus or semantics determined by the phrase
``quantified modal logic.''  A source presentation must specify its
propositional modal base, quantifier rules, domain variation, designation
policy, and local or global consequence.  The clauses below reproduce
Fitting's model and quantifier notation for the limited purpose of comparing
the actualist Barcan schemas; Garson is used only for the surrounding
comparison with other quantified-modal presentations.  No hybrid calculus or
system card is inferred from that semantic example
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998,Garson2001}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-model
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Fitting's varying-domain modal model
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
In Fitting's notation a model is
\[
 \mathcal M=\langle\mathcal G,\mathcal R,\mathcal D,\mathcal I\rangle,
\]
where \(\mathcal G\) is a nonempty set of worlds,
\(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal G^2\), and
\(\mathcal D\) maps each \(\Gamma\in\mathcal G\) to a nonempty world-domain
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The domain of the model is
\(\bigcup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal G}\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The interpretation
\(\mathcal I\) maps each predicate symbol \(P\) to its world-relative
extension \(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)\) over that model domain and each individual
constant \(c\) to a world-indexed denotation
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)\) in the model domain.  A constant is a
\emph{rigid designator} exactly when some \(d\) satisfies
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)=d\) at every world \(\Gamma\).  Rigidity concerns
cross-world identity of denotation; whether \(d\in\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) is the
separate actual-existence question expressed by \(E(c)\).  The Barcan formulas
below contain variables rather than constants, so their proof uses the fixed
valuation convention and does not assume that every name is rigid.
The term is necessary because a world-independent variable assignment does not
fix the denotation policy for names.  Its standing is a property of a constant's
interpretation, and its nonredundancy from existence is used when rigid names
denote objects outside a current world-domain.  For Fitting's special
existence predicate \(E\),
\[
 \mathcal I(E)(\Gamma)=\mathcal D(\Gamma).
\]
Valuations \(v\) take variables into the model domain and do not vary with the
world.  For a formula \(\Phi\), truth is written
\(\mathcal M,\Gamma\forces_v\Phi\).  Ordinary
\((\forall x)\) and \((\exists x)\) are possibilist and range over the whole
model domain.  Fitting's actualist quantifiers are the exact abbreviations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (\forall^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\forall x)[E(x)\supset\Phi],\\
 (\exists^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\exists x)[E(x)\land\Phi].
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the relativized quantifiers range over \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) at world
\(\Gamma\), while modal satisfaction keeps \(v\) fixed when it moves along
\(\mathcal R\).  The model-domain convention is necessary to state
decreasing-domain failures with one world-independent valuation
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Domain regimes and philosophical readings
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
The domains are \emph{constant} when \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) has the same
value at every world; \emph{increasing} when
\(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Delta)\);
\emph{decreasing} when \(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Gamma)\); and
\emph{arbitrarily varying} when no inclusion condition is imposed.  In this
section, \emph{actualist quantification} means Fitting's relativized
\(\forall^E,\exists^E\), while the primitive unrelativized quantifiers are
\emph{possibilist}; and the domain assignment is \emph{necessitist} exactly
when every world-domain is the whole model domain.  These are explicitly defined
interpretations of the semantic parameters, not consequences of the validity
table below.  The displayed BF/CBF table uses the actualist clauses.  Under

generate that table; under necessitism, actualist and possibilist
quantification coincide with the constant-domain case.  This is the later use
that requires the three readings to remain distinct \cite{Williamson2013}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-family
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Quantified modal logic is a parameterized family
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
There is no single calculus or semantics determined by the phrase
``quantified modal logic.''  A source presentation must specify its
propositional modal base, quantifier rules, domain variation, designation
policy, and local or global consequence.  The clauses below reproduce
Fitting's model and quantifier notation for the limited purpose of comparing
the actualist Barcan schemas; Garson is used only for the surrounding
comparison with other quantified-modal presentations.  No hybrid calculus or
system card is inferred from that semantic example
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998,Garson2001}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-model
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Fitting's varying-domain modal model
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
In Fitting's notation a model is
\[
 \mathcal M=\langle\mathcal G,\mathcal R,\mathcal D,\mathcal I\rangle,
\]
where \(\mathcal G\) is a nonempty set of worlds,
\(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal G^2\), and
\(\mathcal D\) maps each \(\Gamma\in\mathcal G\) to a nonempty world-domain
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The domain of the model is
\(\bigcup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal G}\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The interpretation
\(\mathcal I\) maps each predicate symbol \(P\) to its world-relative
extension \(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)\) over that model domain and each individual
constant \(c\) to a world-indexed denotation
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)\) in the model domain.  A constant is a
\emph{rigid designator} exactly when some \(d\) satisfies
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)=d\) at every world \(\Gamma\).  Rigidity concerns
cross-world identity of denotation; whether \(d\in\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) is the
separate actual-existence question expressed by \(E(c)\).  The Barcan formulas
below contain variables rather than constants, so their proof uses the fixed
valuation convention and does not assume that every name is rigid.
The term is necessary because a world-independent variable assignment does not
fix the denotation policy for names.  Its standing is a property of a constant's
interpretation, and its nonredundancy from existence is used when rigid names
denote objects outside a current world-domain.  For Fitting's special
existence predicate \(E\),
\[
 \mathcal I(E)(\Gamma)=\mathcal D(\Gamma).
\]
Valuations \(v\) take variables into the model domain and do not vary with the
world.  For a formula \(\Phi\), truth is written
\(\mathcal M,\Gamma\forces_v\Phi\).  Ordinary
\((\forall x)\) and \((\exists x)\) are possibilist and range over the whole
model domain.  Fitting's actualist quantifiers are the exact abbreviations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (\forall^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\forall x)[E(x)\supset\Phi],\\
 (\exists^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\exists x)[E(x)\land\Phi].
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the relativized quantifiers range over \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) at world
\(\Gamma\), while modal satisfaction keeps \(v\) fixed when it moves along
\(\mathcal R\).  The model-domain convention is necessary to state
decreasing-domain failures with one world-independent valuation
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-qml-domain-regimes
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Domain regimes and philosophical readings
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
The domains are \emph{constant} when \(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) has the same
value at every world; \emph{increasing} when
\(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Delta)\);
\emph{decreasing} when \(\Gamma\mathcal R\Delta\) implies
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)\subseteq\mathcal D(\Gamma)\); and
\emph{arbitrarily varying} when no inclusion condition is imposed.  In this
section, \emph{actualist quantification} means Fitting's relativized
\(\forall^E,\exists^E\), while the primitive unrelativized quantifiers are
\emph{possibilist}; and the domain assignment is \emph{necessitist} exactly
when every world-domain is the whole model domain.  These are explicitly defined
interpretations of the semantic parameters, not consequences of the validity
table below.  The displayed BF/CBF table uses the actualist clauses.  Under
possibilist quantification over the model domain, varying the world-domains does not
generate that table; under necessitism, actualist and possibilist
quantification coincide with the constant-domain case.  This is the later use
that requires the three readings to remain distinct \cite{Williamson2013}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-barcan-schemas
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Barcan and converse Barcan schemas
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For a formula \(\Phi(x)\), the actualist \emph{Barcan formula}
\((\mathrm{BF}^{E})\) and actualist \emph{converse Barcan formula}
\((\mathrm{CBF}^{E})\) in Fitting's notation are respectively
\[
 (\forall^{E}x)\Box\Phi(x)\to\Box(\forall^{E}x)\Phi(x),
 \qquad
 \Box(\forall^{E}x)\Phi(x)\to(\forall^{E}x)\Box\Phi(x).
\]
The superscript records that this table uses the source's actualist
relativization.  With the primitive possibilist quantifier, local-domain
variation does not yield the table below.  The two names remain in this order;
their difference
is used in Table~\ref{tab:p08-barcan-domains} and
Figure~\ref{fig:p08-barcan-countermodel}; they are not interchanged when the
domain convention changes \cite{Barcan1946}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-barcan-domain-validities
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Actualist Barcan validity in Fitting's model
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Under Definitions~\ref{def:p08-qml-model}--\ref{def:p08-barcan-schemas}, the
validity pattern is exactly that displayed in
Table~\ref{tab:p08-barcan-domains}.  The decreasing-domain row uses the fixed
outer domain and fixed-variable-assignment convention; without such a convention the
reversal is not a well-formed comparison.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-barcan-countermodel
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Increasing-domain failure of BF
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Let \(\mathcal G=\{\Gamma,\Delta\}\) and
\(\mathcal R=\{(\Gamma,\Delta)\}\).  Take
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)=\{a\}\),
\(\mathcal D(\Delta)=\{a,b\}\),
\(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)=\varnothing\), and
\(\mathcal I(P)(\Delta)=\{a\}\).  Thus at \(\Delta\), \(P(a)\) is true and
\(P(b)\) is false.  At \(\Gamma\),
\((\forall^{E}x)\Box P(x)\) is true because the sole root-domain
object \(a\) satisfies \(P\) at the accessible world.  But
\(\Box(\forall^{E}x)P(x)\) is false because the new object
\(b\in\mathcal D(\Delta)\) fails \(P\) there.  Thus the model refutes
\(\mathrm{BF}^{E}\).  It does not refute \(\mathrm{CBF}^{E}\).

policy, and local or global consequence.  The clauses below reproduce
Fitting's model and quantifier notation for the limited purpose of comparing
the actualist Barcan schemas; Garson is used only for the surrounding
comparison with other quantified-modal presentations.  No hybrid calculus or

\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998,Garson2001}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-qml-model
current_declaration_bindings.title: Fitting's varying-domain modal model
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
In Fitting's notation a model is
\[
 \mathcal M=\langle\mathcal G,\mathcal R,\mathcal D,\mathcal I\rangle,
\]
where \(\mathcal G\) is a nonempty set of worlds,
\(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal G^2\), and
\(\mathcal D\) maps each \(\Gamma\in\mathcal G\) to a nonempty world-domain
\(\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The domain of the model is
\(\bigcup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal G}\mathcal D(\Gamma)\).  The interpretation
\(\mathcal I\) maps each predicate symbol \(P\) to its world-relative
extension \(\mathcal I(P)(\Gamma)\) over that model domain and each individual
constant \(c\) to a world-indexed denotation
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)\) in the model domain.  A constant is a
\emph{rigid designator} exactly when some \(d\) satisfies
\(\mathcal I(c)(\Gamma)=d\) at every world \(\Gamma\).  Rigidity concerns
cross-world identity of denotation; whether \(d\in\mathcal D(\Gamma)\) is the
separate actual-existence question expressed by \(E(c)\).  The Barcan formulas
below contain variables rather than constants, so their proof uses the fixed
valuation convention and does not assume that every name is rigid.
The term is necessary because a world-independent variable assignment does not
fix the denotation policy for names.  Its standing is a property of a constant's
interpretation, and its nonredundancy from existence is used when rigid names
denote objects outside a current world-domain.  For Fitting's special
existence predicate \(E\),
\[
 \mathcal I(E)(\Gamma)=\mathcal D(\Gamma).
\]
Valuations \(v\) take variables into the model domain and do not vary with the
world.  For a formula \(\Phi\), truth is written
\(\mathcal M,\Gamma\forces_v\Phi\).  Ordinary
\((\forall x)\) and \((\exists x)\) are possibilist and range over the whole
model domain.  Fitting's actualist quantifiers are the exact abbreviations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (\forall^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\forall x)[E(x)\supset\Phi],\\
 (\exists^{E}x)\Phi
 &\defeq (\exists x)[E(x)\land\Phi].
\end{aligned}
\]

\(\Gamma\), while modal satisfaction keeps \(v\) fixed when it moves along
\(\mathcal R\).  The model-domain convention is necessary to state
decreasing-domain failures with one world-independent valuation
\cite{Fitting2002Alethic,FittingMendelsohn1998}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-negative-free-logic
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Negative free-logic semantics
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Fix a nonempty outer domain \(D^{\mathrm{out}}\), a nonempty existing domain
\(D^{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq D^{\mathrm{out}}\), and a total interpretation of
individual constants and function symbols into \(D^{\mathrm{out}}\).  In the
selected \emph{negative free-logic semantics}, each \(n\)-ary predicate has
extension contained in \((D^{\mathrm{in}})^n\),
\(E!(t)\) is true exactly when the value of \(t\) belongs to
\(D^{\mathrm{in}}\), and strict identity \(r=t\) is true exactly when both
term values exist and are the same object.  Quantifiers range over
\(D^{\mathrm{in}}\).  Hence every atom containing a denoting but nonexisting
outer-domain object is false; this is not called ``non-denotation.''

The adjective ``negative'' is necessary because positive free logic permits
some true predications of nonexisting objects, while a neutral partial
semantics can assign a truth-value gap when a term has no value.  It names one
two-valued model class, not all free logics.  Its strict atomic and equality
clauses distinguish it from the two exact variants in the table below and are
used by the guarded quantifier rules and description policy
\cite{Lambert1967,Bencivenga1986}.
\index{free logic}\index{negative free logic}\index{existence predicate}

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-free-logic-consequence
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Variant-indexed free-logic consequence
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For \(v\in\{\mathrm{neg},\mathrm{pos},\mathrm{neu}\}\), write
\(\Gamma\models_v A\) when every model of the corresponding row of
Table~\ref{tab:p08-free-logic-variants} that designates every member of
\(\Gamma\) also designates \(A\).  In the negative and positive rows,
designation is ordinary truth; in the neutral row, only
\(\mathsf t\) is designated.  These are three typed semantic consequence
relations, not one family-wide proof calculus.  The subscripts are necessary
because the atomic and partial-term policies differ, and they are used in the
quantifier-rule table below.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-distributed-knowledge
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Distributed knowledge for a finite group
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Let \(G\subseteq I\) be nonempty and finite.  In the multi-agent epistemic
model with agent relations \(\sim_i\), define
\[
 R_G^{D}\defeq\bigcap_{i\in G}\sim_i,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M,w\models D_GA
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \forall u\,(wR_G^{D}u\Rightarrow\mathcal M,u\models A).
\]
The name is necessary because pooled information can determine \(A\) even
when no individual agent knows it.  It names a group modality, not a new frame
relation for an individual agent.  It differs from
\(E_GA\defeq\bigwedge_{i\in G}K_iA\), which uses the union of one-step agent
alternatives, and from \(C_GA\), which uses the reflexive--transitive closure
of that union.  The distinction is used by the card and comparison table below
\cite{FaginHalpernMosesVardi1995}.
\index{distributed knowledge}\index{group knowledge}

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-common-knowledge-noncompact
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Common knowledge and noncompactness
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Let \(G\) contain at least two agents, put \(E_G^0p=p\), and put
\(E_G^{n+1}p=E_GE_G^np\).  Then
\[
 \{E_G^np:n\in\mathbb N\}\entails_{\mathsf{S5}_{I}^{C}} C_Gp,
\]
but no finite subset of the premise set entails \(C_Gp\).  Consequently the
finitary sheet can be weakly complete for valid formulas but not strongly
complete for arbitrary premise sets.  The group-size hypothesis is essential:
for one \(\mathsf{S5}\) agent the iterations collapse.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-muddy-children
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Muddy children under a fixed public protocol
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Suppose \(n\) children see all other foreheads but not their own, exactly
\(k\ge1\) are muddy, the truthful statement that at least one child is muddy is
public, questions are synchronous, and every negative answer is truthful and
public.  The muddy children first know that they are muddy at round \(k\),
after \(k-1\) public rounds of all-negative answers.  The conclusion depends on
all of these information and timing hypotheses; it is not a consequence of the
bare fact that \(k\) children are muddy.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-distributed-knowledge
current_declaration_bindings.title: Distributed knowledge for a finite group
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Let \(G\subseteq I\) be nonempty and finite.  In the multi-agent epistemic
model with agent relations \(\sim_i\), define
\[
 R_G^{D}\defeq\bigcap_{i\in G}\sim_i,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M,w\models D_GA
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \forall u\,(wR_G^{D}u\Rightarrow\mathcal M,u\models A).
\]
The name is necessary because pooled information can determine \(A\) even
when no individual agent knows it.  It names a group modality, not a new frame
relation for an individual agent.  It differs from
\(E_GA\defeq\bigwedge_{i\in G}K_iA\), which uses the union of one-step agent
alternatives, and from \(C_GA\), which uses the reflexive--transitive closure
of that union.  The distinction is used by the card and comparison table below
\cite{FaginHalpernMosesVardi1995}.
\index{distributed knowledge}\index{group knowledge}

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-common-knowledge-noncompact
current_declaration_bindings.title: Common knowledge and noncompactness
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Let \(G\) contain at least two agents, put \(E_G^0p=p\), and put
\(E_G^{n+1}p=E_GE_G^np\).  Then
\[
 \{E_G^np:n\in\mathbb N\}\entails_{\mathsf{S5}_{I}^{C}} C_Gp,
\]
but no finite subset of the premise set entails \(C_Gp\).  Consequently the
finitary sheet can be weakly complete for valid formulas but not strongly
complete for arbitrary premise sets.  The group-size hypothesis is essential:
for one \(\mathsf{S5}\) agent the iterations collapse.

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-muddy-children
current_declaration_bindings.title: Muddy children under a fixed public protocol
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Suppose \(n\) children see all other foreheads but not their own, exactly
\(k\ge1\) are muddy, the truthful statement that at least one child is muddy is
public, questions are synchronous, and every negative answer is truthful and
public.  The muddy children first know that they are muddy at round \(k\),
after \(k-1\) public rounds of all-negative answers.  The conclusion depends on
all of these information and timing hypotheses; it is not a consequence of the
bare fact that \(k\) children are muddy.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-public-announcement
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Truthful public-announcement update
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
For an epistemic structure \(\mathcal M\), let
\(\mathcal M\mathbin{\upharpoonright}\chi\) be the substructure induced by the worlds where
\(\chi\) is true.  The public-announcement modality has the clause
\[
 \mathcal M,w\entails[!\chi]A
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \bigl(\mathcal M,w\not\entails\chi\ \lor\
       \mathcal M\mathbin{\upharpoonright}\chi,w\entails A\bigr),
\]
and \(\langle!\chi\rangle A\defeq\neg[!\chi]\neg A\).  The update is a
model restriction, not a change to the valuation at surviving worlds.  Its
standing and vacuous-failure clause distinguish announcement from ordinary
knowledge and are used by the reduction theorem and the unsuccessful-update
example.  General event-model product update is broader and is not identified
with this operation \cite{Plaza1989,BaltagMossSolecki1998}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: thm:p08-pal-reduction
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Reduction of public announcements
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Over the exact finite-agent \(\mathsf{S5}_{I}\) base fixed by
\hyperref[sheet:hilbert-s5n]{\texttt{sheet:hilbert-s5n}}, every public-announcement
formula is provably equivalent, using
\hyperref[sheet:hilbert-pal]{\texttt{sheet:hilbert-pal}}, to an
announcement-free epistemic formula.  Hence the reduction calculus is sound
and complete for the update semantics of
Definition~\ref{def:p08-public-announcement}.  This does not reduce arbitrary
action-model logic to the same static language
\cite{VanDitmarschVanDerHoekKooi2007}.

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-unsuccessful-announcement
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: An unsuccessful truthful update
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Call \(\chi\) \emph{successful} when \([!\chi]\chi\) is valid.  This is a
metalinguistic property of an announcement formula, needed to distinguish
preservation of announced content from mere executability; it is not another
modality, differs from truth before an update, and is used in this example.
Let two worlds \(w,v\) be indistinguishable to agent \(i\), with \(p\) true
only at \(w\).  At \(w\), \(\chi=p\land\neg K_ip\) is true.  Restricting to
the \(\chi\)-world leaves only \(w\), where \(K_ip\) is now true, so \(\chi\)
is false after its own truthful announcement.  Thus truth before update does
not entail success \cite{VanDitmarschVanDerHoekKooi2007}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-public-announcement
current_declaration_bindings.title: Truthful public-announcement update
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
For an epistemic structure \(\mathcal M\), let
\(\mathcal M\mathbin{\upharpoonright}\chi\) be the substructure induced by the worlds where
\(\chi\) is true.  The public-announcement modality has the clause
\[
 \mathcal M,w\entails[!\chi]A
 \quad\text{ iff }\quad
 \bigl(\mathcal M,w\not\entails\chi\ \lor\
       \mathcal M\mathbin{\upharpoonright}\chi,w\entails A\bigr),
\]
and \(\langle!\chi\rangle A\defeq\neg[!\chi]\neg A\).  The update is a
model restriction, not a change to the valuation at surviving worlds.  Its
standing and vacuous-failure clause distinguish announcement from ordinary
knowledge and are used by the reduction theorem and the unsuccessful-update
example.  General event-model product update is broader and is not identified
with this operation \cite{Plaza1989,BaltagMossSolecki1998}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: thm:p08-pal-reduction
current_declaration_bindings.title: Reduction of public announcements
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Over the exact finite-agent \(\mathsf{S5}_{I}\) base fixed by
\hyperref[sheet:hilbert-s5n]{\texttt{sheet:hilbert-s5n}}, every public-announcement
formula is provably equivalent, using
\hyperref[sheet:hilbert-pal]{\texttt{sheet:hilbert-pal}}, to an
announcement-free epistemic formula.  Hence the reduction calculus is sound
and complete for the update semantics of
Definition~\ref{def:p08-public-announcement}.  This does not reduce arbitrary
action-model logic to the same static language
\cite{VanDitmarschVanDerHoekKooi2007}.

current_declaration_bindings.label: def:p08-unsuccessful-announcement
current_declaration_bindings.title: An unsuccessful truthful update
current_declaration_bindings.declaration_text:
Call \(\chi\) \emph{successful} when \([!\chi]\chi\) is valid.  This is a
metalinguistic property of an announcement formula, needed to distinguish
preservation of announced content from mere executability; it is not another
modality, differs from truth before an update, and is used in this example.
Let two worlds \(w,v\) be indistinguishable to agent \(i\), with \(p\) true
only at \(w\).  At \(w\), \(\chi=p\land\neg K_ip\) is true.  Restricting to
the \(\chi\)-world leaves only \(w\), where \(K_ip\) is now true, so \(\chi\)
is false after its own truthful announcement.  Thus truth before update does
not entail success \cite{VanDitmarschVanDerHoekKooi2007}.

In [temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex:332](C:/Dev/the-methods-of-reason/handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex:332), the CTL computation-tree root label changed from \(w\) to \(w:\neg p\). The node identifier, edges, two infinite branch continuations, four annotations, caption and stable label fig:p08-ctl-tree remain unchanged.

The actual [total-transition definition, lines 46–55](C:/Dev/the-methods-of-reason/handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex:46) requires a nonempty state set, a successor at every state, and paths indexed from zero. The [CTL clauses, lines 69–99](C:/Dev/the-methods-of-reason/handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex:69) make EX/AX existential/universal over immediate successors and permit a strong-until witness at index zero. The [registered EF/AF equations, lines 5–6](C:/Dev/the-methods-of-reason/handbook/registry/calculi/hilbert-ctl.tex:5) identify eventuality with until having the always-true left operand. These current passages were read; no new primary-paper fidelity claim is made.

- The prerequisite at handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex lines 46--55 requires a nonempty carrier, total binary relation, typed valuation, and infinite paths. Lines 58--104 give the host CTL state grammar and strong-until semantics; lines 129--164 give the mutually typed CTL* state/path grammar and semantics. The N-c-016 bridge respects each of these domains and ownership rules.

2. **`handbook/parts/p09/presentations/n-c-016.tex:1521-1547` — the claimed Baier--Katoen/host bridge is only a graph bridge, not yet a well-typed semantic bridge.** The prerequisite definition at `handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex:46-55` requires a valuation \(V:\mathsf{Prop}\to\mathcal P(S)\), but line 1523 defines \(V_0:AP\to2^S\) and lines 1528-1540 call \((S,R_0,V_0)\) a structure of the host type without identifying \(AP\) with \(\mathsf{Prop}\) or extending \(V_0\). Lines 1543-1547 then use an undeclared Baier--Katoen metavariable \(\Phi\) before its grammar at lines 1567-1576 and place that same glyph on both sides of a semantic equivalence even though the source constructors \(\exists\bigcirc,\forall\bigcirc,\exists U,\forall U\) and the host constructors \(\mathsf{EX},\mathsf{AX},\mathsf E[U],\mathsf A[U]\) are not literally the same syntax. Consequently the displayed induction does not yet justify the later claim that Method~`def:p09-ctl-labelling` is instantiated. **Minimal repair:** explicitly take the host proposition alphabet to be \(AP\) (or give a total extension of \(V_0\)); then either identify each source constructor with its host counterpart

The inherited host definition at `handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex`, lines 46--53, defines a total transition structure only for \(S\ne\varnothing\).  The N-c-016 text itself recognizes this boundary at lines 1597--1602: \(\mathcal K_0\) is of the host method's type when \(S\ne\varnothing\), and the host method is not instantiated when \(S=\varnothing\).  The unqualified claim at lines 1587--1589 is therefore false in exactly the empty-source case that the following paragraph deliberately retains.

- `handbook/parts/p08/temporal-epistemic-supplement.tex`, lines 35--185, supplies the inherited CTL/CTL* typing.  In particular, lines 46--53 require \(S\ne\varnothing\) for the host total transition structure.  That exact inherited requirement controls both must-fixes.

existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Standard deontic logic
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Standard deontic logic \(\mathsf{SDL}\) is normal modal logic \(\mathsf{KD}\)
with \(O A\) read as ``it ought to be that \(A\)'' and
\(\mathsf P_O A\defeq\neg O\neg A\). Relationally, \(O\) is box over a serial
ideal-alternative relation. The name is necessary to fix this monadic normal
system rather than deontic logic generally. It stands as a formal modal
calculus/semantics, differs through seriality and the D axiom
\(OA\to\mathsf P_OA\), and is used as the baseline for contrary-to-duty failures
\cite{VonWright1951,McNamara2006}.
\index{standard deontic logic}\index{obligation operator}\index{permission operator}

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-dyadic-obligation
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Best-world semantics for dyadic obligation
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
A dyadic deontic model adds, at each world \(w\), a total preorder
\(\preceq_w\) on
\(R(w)=\{u\in W:wRu\}\), oriented so that
\(u\preceq_w v\) means that \(u\) is at least as ideal as \(v\).  Its strict
part is
\[
 u\prec_w v
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\preceq_w v\ \text{and}\ v\not\preceq_w u.
\]
The preorder is \emph{smooth on definable candidate sets} when, for every
formula \(B\) and every \(u\in R(w)\cap[B]\), either no member of
\(R(w)\cap[B]\) is strictly more ideal than \(u\), or there is
\(v\in R(w)\cap[B]\) such that \(v\prec_w u\) and no
\(z\in R(w)\cap[B]\) satisfies \(z\prec_w v\).  Define, for every \(B\),
\[
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)
 =\{u\in R(w)\cap[B]:
       \nexists v\in R(w)\cap[B]\ (v\prec_w u)\}.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Best}_w(B)=\varnothing\) when there is no accessible
\(B\)-world, while smoothness makes it nonempty whenever the candidate set is
nonempty.  Put
\[
 M,w\models O(A\mid B)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\subseteq[A].
\]
The existence conjunct makes an obligation with an impossible condition false
in this selected presentation; a vacuous alternative would be a different
dyadic semantics.
The name is necessary because \(B\) is a parameter of the ideality comparison,
not the antecedent of material implication.  It names a binary modality under
the displayed preference semantics, not dyadic deontic logic in general.  It
differs from \(O(B\to A)\) and is used to state
\(O(\neg B\mid\neg A)\) as a violation-triggered obligation without detaching
it in ideal \(A\)-worlds \cite{Hansson1969}.
\index{dyadic deontic logic}\index{conditional obligation}

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-sdl
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Standard deontic logic
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
Standard deontic logic \(\mathsf{SDL}\) is normal modal logic \(\mathsf{KD}\)
with \(O A\) read as ``it ought to be that \(A\)'' and
\(\mathsf P_O A\defeq\neg O\neg A\). Relationally, \(O\) is box over a serial
ideal-alternative relation. The name is necessary to fix this monadic normal
system rather than deontic logic generally. It stands as a formal modal
calculus/semantics, differs through seriality and the D axiom
\(OA\to\mathsf P_OA\), and is used as the baseline for contrary-to-duty failures
\cite{VonWright1951,McNamara2006}.
\index{standard deontic logic}\index{obligation operator}\index{permission operator}

existing_common_goal_anchors.label: def:p08-dyadic-obligation
existing_common_goal_anchors.title: Best-world semantics for dyadic obligation
existing_common_goal_anchors.declaration_text:
A dyadic deontic model adds, at each world \(w\), a total preorder
\(\preceq_w\) on
\(R(w)=\{u\in W:wRu\}\), oriented so that
\(u\preceq_w v\) means that \(u\) is at least as ideal as \(v\).  Its strict
part is
\[
 u\prec_w v
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\preceq_w v\ \text{and}\ v\not\preceq_w u.
\]
The preorder is \emph{smooth on definable candidate sets} when, for every
formula \(B\) and every \(u\in R(w)\cap[B]\), either no member of
\(R(w)\cap[B]\) is strictly more ideal than \(u\), or there is
\(v\in R(w)\cap[B]\) such that \(v\prec_w u\) and no
\(z\in R(w)\cap[B]\) satisfies \(z\prec_w v\).  Define, for every \(B\),
\[
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)
 =\{u\in R(w)\cap[B]:
       \nexists v\in R(w)\cap[B]\ (v\prec_w u)\}.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Best}_w(B)=\varnothing\) when there is no accessible
\(B\)-world, while smoothness makes it nonempty whenever the candidate set is
nonempty.  Put
\[
 M,w\models O(A\mid B)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\subseteq[A].
\]
The existence conjunct makes an obligation with an impossible condition false
in this selected presentation; a vacuous alternative would be a different
dyadic semantics.
The name is necessary because \(B\) is a parameter of the ideality comparison,
not the antecedent of material implication.  It names a binary modality under
the displayed preference semantics, not dyadic deontic logic in general.  It
differs from \(O(B\to A)\) and is used to state
\(O(\neg B\mid\neg A)\) as a violation-triggered obligation without detaching
it in ideal \(A\)-worlds \cite{Hansson1969}.
\index{dyadic deontic logic}\index{conditional obligation}

 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\subseteq[A].

in this selected presentation; a vacuous alternative would be a different
dyadic semantics.

not the antecedent of material implication.  It names a binary modality under
the displayed preference semantics, not dyadic deontic logic in general.  It
differs from \(O(B\to A)\) and is used to state
\(O(\neg B\mid\neg A)\) as a violation-triggered obligation without detaching

present_destinations.label: def:p08-sdl
present_destinations.title: Standard deontic logic
present_destinations.declaration_text:
Standard deontic logic \(\mathsf{SDL}\) is normal modal logic \(\mathsf{KD}\)
with \(O A\) read as ``it ought to be that \(A\)'' and
\(\mathsf P_O A\defeq\neg O\neg A\). Relationally, \(O\) is box over a serial
ideal-alternative relation. The name is necessary to fix this monadic normal
system rather than deontic logic generally. It stands as a formal modal
calculus/semantics, differs through seriality and the D axiom
\(OA\to\mathsf P_OA\), and is used as the baseline for contrary-to-duty failures
\cite{VonWright1951,McNamara2006}.
\index{standard deontic logic}\index{obligation operator}\index{permission operator}

present_destinations.label: def:p08-dyadic-obligation
present_destinations.title: Best-world semantics for dyadic obligation
present_destinations.declaration_text:
A dyadic deontic model adds, at each world \(w\), a total preorder
\(\preceq_w\) on
\(R(w)=\{u\in W:wRu\}\), oriented so that
\(u\preceq_w v\) means that \(u\) is at least as ideal as \(v\).  Its strict
part is
\[
 u\prec_w v
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u\preceq_w v\ \text{and}\ v\not\preceq_w u.
\]
The preorder is \emph{smooth on definable candidate sets} when, for every
formula \(B\) and every \(u\in R(w)\cap[B]\), either no member of
\(R(w)\cap[B]\) is strictly more ideal than \(u\), or there is
\(v\in R(w)\cap[B]\) such that \(v\prec_w u\) and no
\(z\in R(w)\cap[B]\) satisfies \(z\prec_w v\).  Define, for every \(B\),
\[
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)
 =\{u\in R(w)\cap[B]:
       \nexists v\in R(w)\cap[B]\ (v\prec_w u)\}.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Best}_w(B)=\varnothing\) when there is no accessible
\(B\)-world, while smoothness makes it nonempty whenever the candidate set is
nonempty.  Put
\[
 M,w\models O(A\mid B)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Best}_w(B)\subseteq[A].
\]
The existence conjunct makes an obligation with an impossible condition false
in this selected presentation; a vacuous alternative would be a different
dyadic semantics.
The name is necessary because \(B\) is a parameter of the ideality comparison,
not the antecedent of material implication.  It names a binary modality under
the displayed preference semantics, not dyadic deontic logic in general.  It
differs from \(O(B\to A)\) and is used to state
\(O(\neg B\mid\neg A)\) as a violation-triggered obligation without detaching
it in ideal \(A\)-worlds \cite{Hansson1969}.
\index{dyadic deontic logic}\index{conditional obligation}
